sections.title: Jó + time of day
sections.content: Hungarian greetings follow the pattern "jó" (good) plus a time of day. *Jó reggelt* covers the early morning, *jó napot* is the all-purpose daytime greeting once morning has passed, and *jó estét* takes over in the evening. All three work as both "hello" and, less commonly, "goodbye" for that part of the day.

*Jó napot* is the safest default if you're ever unsure which one fits — Hungarians reach for it constantly, from mid-morning right through the afternoon, in shops, on the phone, with strangers on the street.
